archetype: Explorer bow damage dealer built around a keydown main attack (Hurricane). Because the damage engine is a held-key channel rather than discrete casts, the class does not gain from the highest attack-speed brackets the way burst classes do, and its progression is unusually front-loaded onto a small number of 4th job skills (Hurricane, Final Attack, Arrow Blaster, Arrow Stream) that boost nodes and HEXA Mastery cores both target. Weapon multiplier 1.3x per Grandis Library. The class carries a large amount of Ignore DEF and Critical Rate from its own passives, which changes what it needs from gear and Inner Ability relative to other Explorers.

The class doc's operative sentence is: 'It is mandatory to level the first four nodes to maximum. Node 5 for Covering Fire/Swift Surge is optional for mains looking to minmax and not necessary for 6th job progression. Node 6 is completely useless at all times.' Grandis Library buckets the same six groups as Primary (Nodes 1-2), Secondary (Nodes 3-4) and Other (Nodes 5-6). The array below is therefore ordered by node group, and that order IS stated by the sources.

vMatrix.notes: What every source agrees on is the node-group shape, not the trios: Nodes 1-4 are taken to max before anything else, Node 5 is a minmax-only extra, Node 6 is dead. That is the safe advice to give a player. Exact trio pairings are the weakest part of the public Bow Master record: the class doc encodes them in images, Grandis Library only publishes node groups and Primary/Secondary/Other buckets rather than pairings, and the only explicit written trios come from a source whose data is stated as 2024-05-14 and therefore predates the v269 boost-node grouping changes that Grandis Library's own 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle is evidence of. Do not present trio pairings with the same confidence as the node-group order. Also note for consensus maths: Grandis Library's Credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc', so Grandis is a mirror of the class doc for node priority - it is NOT a second vote.

observedBoostNodes.source: in-game V Matrix tooltips, Archerroni Lv 245, GMS Heroic
observedBoostNodes.note: Read straight off the player's own matrix, which outranks any guide: these are the six boost nodes that exist for this class, with their exact names and the skills each one pairs. Levels are this player's, not a recommendation.
observedBoostNodes.perLevelFinalDamage: Not uniform across skills. At level 1: Wind Arrow +5%, Covering Fire / Swift Surge / Arrow Blow +3%, Gritty Gust / Speed Mirage +2%. At level 7 the Quiver Cartridge node gives Magic Arrow +14% (2%/level) and Phoenix +21% (3%/level). So node value depends on WHICH skills it pairs, not just its level - a boost node ranking that ignores that is ranking the wrong thing.

hexa.notes: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FACT, and the most product-relevant thing in this file: the class doc does not publish a single flat HEXA order. It publishes separate priority charts chosen along two axes. Axis one is server type - quoting the doc, 'Heroic World players should pick from the FRAGMENT LIMITED charts listed first and Interactive World players who are using the market to buy fragments when necessary should use the ENERGY LIMITED charts below that.' Axis two is what the character is for, with three variants the doc heads MAIN/MIN CLEAR PRIORITY, LEGION CHAMP PRIORITY and BURST/CULVERT PRIORITY. Grandis Library publishes three 6th Job infographics under the headings '6th Job (Main/Min-Clear)', '6th Job (Legion Champ)' and '6th Job (Mule/Culvert)' - the same three-way split, with the third named differently (Mule/Culvert vs Burst/Culvert). Note that Grandis is not an independent vote here, but the infographic set does confirm the three-way split is the class's own published shape. A planner that emits one universal Bow Master HEXA order is therefore contradicting the class's own maintained guide. The detailed step-by-step sequences live inside those images and did not survive text extraction, so per-step target levels are NOT recorded here - only the category order above, which came from the doc's prose. Anyone completing this file should read the infographics directly.

hyperStats.notes: The class doc declines to publish a fixed hyper stat order on the grounds that the optimal allocation depends on the character's own stat sheet, and points readers at a calculator instead: 'A popular hyper stat calculator can be found here for optimizations: https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/'. That refusal is itself the finding and should be surfaced to users rather than papered over with a static list: the community's operative answer to Bow Master hyper stat priority is a per-character optimizer, not a ranking. The one thing a planner SHOULD assert for this class is the Critical Rate overflow rule, because a generic optimizer preset that hard-caps crit at 100% will get Bow Master wrong.

gearingNotes:
Bow Master changes gearing advice in four specific ways, all sourced to the class doc unless noted.

1. CRITICAL RATE DOES NOT STOP AT 100%. Vicious Shot allows Critical Rate to exceed the cap and converts total Critical Rate into Critical Damage at a 50% ratio. Grandis Library independently lists the skill as granting 50% of Critical Rate. Practical consequence: keep buying crit rate past the point where other classes stop - the class doc suggests roughly 7-10 extra hyper stat points late game - and do not let a planner or optimizer hard-cap crit at 100% for this class.

2. NO IED LINES ON WEAPON, SECONDARY OR EMBLEM. The class doc states Bow Master's own passives already supply enough Ignore DEF that IED lines on WSE are not needed, and recommends a 9/0/0 attack/boss/IED main potential loadout instead. The two sources disagree on how much IED the passives actually give - the class doc cites two passives contributing 40% and 25%, while Grandis Library's base-stats-from-skills summary totals 59.85% Ignore DEF - so the exact number is contested, but both agree it is large.

3. NO COOLDOWN HAT. The class doc says to stack %DEX on the hat rather than taking a cooldown-reduction hat. This is a real fork for players coming from classes where the cooldown hat is standard.

4. ATTACK SPEED CAPS EARLY. As a keydown class it does not benefit from the highest attack speed bracket; the class doc puts the useful natural cap at 8 from gear. This removes the attack speed inner ability line and de-prioritises attack speed sources generally.

Other sourced gearing facts from the class doc: Titanium Arrows give +9 attack and only a single arrow needs to be held in the inventory; Blood Arrows cost roughly 4% damage relative to Magic Arrows and should only be used when the sustain is actually needed; Ring of Restraint and Continuous Ring are both kept equipped; the Legion grid is ranked Critical Damage > Boss Damage > IED = Critical Rate > DEX > ATT > Buff Duration. The class doc also names an endgame secondary weapon and emblem, but those item names could not be validated against a skill/item table in this session and are deliberately omitted rather than risk printing a wrong item name.

commonMistakes.mistake: Capping Critical Rate at 100% and moving points elsewhere
commonMistakes.why: Vicious Shot converts total Critical Rate into Critical Damage at 50%, so overflow crit is still damage on this class specifically.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying IED lines on weapon, secondary and emblem
commonMistakes.why: Class passives already supply a large IED total; the class doc directs those potential lines to attack instead.
The class doc directs the hat to %DEX instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Chasing attack speed 10 or rolling the attack speed inner ability line
commonMistakes.why: Keydown attack, so the top attack speed bracket does not convert into damage; the useful cap is reached from gear. The class doc lists Attack Speed +1 among the lines Bow Master does not need, and Grandis Library's Attack Speed page independently states that Hurricane-type / key-down skills are not affected by Attack Speed.
The class doc measures roughly a 4% damage loss versus Magic Arrows; it is a sustain tool, not a default.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on Arrow Blaster on a high-ping connection
commonMistakes.why: The class doc records that the skill performs poorly at high ping, which affects both node and rotation choices.

commonMistakes.mistake: Following a single universal HEXA order
commonMistakes.why: The class's own guide splits HEXA priority charts by server type (Fragment-limited for Heroic World, Energy-limited for Interactive World) and by character role (MAIN/MIN CLEAR, LEGION CHAMP, BURST/CULVERT). Grandis Library mirrors the same three-way split in its infographic set. A one-size order contradicts the source.

commonMistakes.mistake: Partially leveling Sol Hecate and stopping between breakpoints
commonMistakes.why: Its abilities unlock at specific levels - the summon and Styx at Lv. 1, Charon at Lv. 20, Phlegethon at Lv. 30 - so levels spent between breakpoints buy comparatively little.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating the class doc's hyper stat 'big 4' as a ranked order
commonMistakes.why: The class doc explicitly declines to rank hyper stats and names Crit Damage, IED, Boss and Damage as an unordered group, pointing readers at a per-character calculator. A planner that reads them as a fixed order is asserting something the source refuses to say.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionMethod: Scope narrowed by the product owner to the five endgame sections (vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility). Each in-scope defect was settled by re-opening the exact cited page and re-reading the exact disputed claim. No new source discovery was performed except where a cited source was unreachable.
defects: UNSETTLED (recorded as a conflict, not a claim): which skill the 'Final Attack' boost node targets. Grandis Library's node list says 'Final Attack: Bow (2nd Job)'; the class doc says 'Advanced Final Attack'; MapleStory Wiki confirms these are two distinct co-existing skills with a prerequisite relationship. Cannot be settled from any reachable text source - the class doc's node membership is image-encoded. Requires a vision pass on the class doc's boost node infographic.

UNSETTLED (recorded as a conflict, not a claim): the class doc's own Node 1-4 skill membership. Three text extractions of the same image region this session returned three mutually inconsistent readings. The file uses Grandis Library's plain-text pairing and flags the choice. Requires the same vision pass.

resolved.defect: The merged node entry 'Final Attack (class doc writes Advanced Final Attack; Grandis Library writes Final Attack: Bow)' and the matching conflict entry assert an identity no source states, and Grandis contradicts it.
resolved.whatWasDone: The asserted identity was deleted. MapleStory Wiki's Advanced Final Attack page was checked and confirms Advanced Final Attack is a 4th job passive requiring Final Attack: Bow (MAX) - two distinct skills, not aliases. The vMatrix Node 1 entry now records both source strings side by side with an explicit 'source strings differ' marker and no identity claim. boostNodeTargets no longer ships a single canonical string for this node; it carries both with 'UNRESOLVED - do not emit either as canonical yet'. The conflict entry was rewritten and marked status: unresolved.

resolved.defect: archetype asserts four 4th job skills and that boost nodes and HEXA Mastery cores target the same set; per Grandis, Arrow Blaster is 3rd Job and Final Attack: Bow is 2nd Job.
resolved.scope: OUT OF SCOPE - job tiers, explicitly excluded by the product owner's scope narrowing
resolved.whatWasDone: Counted as out-of-scope and the archetype text was not modified, per the instruction to leave job-tier content alone. For the record, the re-read does show the overlap claim is close but not exact: the class doc's Mastery core list covers Hurricane, Arrow Stream, Arrow Blaster, Quiver Cartridge, Phoenix, Speed Mirage and Gritty Gust, with no Mastery core for the Final Attack node target.

resolved.defect: The bossing-trio conflict note reasons that 'Erda Nova is a 5th job skill and boost nodes target 4th job skills' - a false premise, since Grandis's node list contains 1st through 4th job and Hyper skills.
resolved.whatWasDone: The false premise was deleted. Re-reading Grandis confirms the defect: its Bow Master node list labels Arrow Blow '1st Job', Final Attack: Bow / Quiver Cartridge / Covering Fire / Swift Surge / Wind Arrow '2nd Job', Arrow Blaster / Phoenix / Speed Mirage '3rd Job', Hurricane / Arrow Stream '4th Job' and Gritty Gust 'Hyper Skill'. The conclusion (Erda Nova is an extraction artifact) is retained on a sound basis: it appears in no node list from any reachable source, and the extraction that produced it also produced two other mutually inconsistent readings of the same image region.

resolved.defect: 'Extra Quiver Cartridge' appears in no reachable source and is a probable extraction artifact.
resolved.disposition: CONFIRMED THE NAME IS REAL, CORRECTED ITS PLACEMENT
resolved.whatWasDone: The defect is refuted on existence: MapleStory Wiki carries a page at /w/Extra_Quiver_Cartridge describing it as an active Bow Master skill, max level 30, granted by the 6th Job Mastery Enhancement that also upgrades Quiver Cartridge and Phoenix. The class doc independently describes its mechanic. However the file's PLACEMENT was wrong: it was listed as a third Mastery core to invest in alongside Quiver Cartridge VI and Phoenix VI. It has been removed from hexa.order group 3 and from skillNameReference.hexaMastery, and moved to a new skillNameReference.grantedByMasteryCore entry that states the correct relationship. The wiki page returns 403 to direct fetching; verification was via a web-search result summary of that exact URL and the verificationMethod is recorded on the claim.

resolved.defect: 'Flashpoint' as the Ascent skill is single-sourced to a text extraction; Grandis's 6th Job section lists only Ascendant Shadow, yet hexa.order presents Flashpoint flatly as 'Second HEXA node'.
resolved.whatWasDone: The name is corroborated - Grandis Library ships a skill-preview icon asset at /class-icons/explorers/bowmaster/flashpoint.png - but Grandis never names it in descriptive text and never identifies it as the Ascent skill, confirming the defect on the ROLE claim. The hexa.order entry now states plainly that the role and the second-node position are single-sourced to the class doc, with sourceCount 1 and consensus weak, and carries a sourceCountNote spelling out exactly what Grandis does and does not corroborate. Two unverifiable details attached to that entry ('six key presses', '4 minute cooldown outside boss content') were DELETED - they could not be found on re-reading.

resolved.defect: hyperStats.priority is an ordered array while the class doc explicitly declines to rank hyper stats, and the Critical Damage entry justifies first place using the Legion grid, a different system.
resolved.whatWasDone: Fully confirmed on re-read. The class doc says 'Hyper stats are largely dependent on your own individual stats and what your character needs' and names 'the usual big 4 of Crit Damage, IED, Boss, and Damage' as an unordered group. hyperStats.priority is now null, with priorityIsNullBecause explaining why, an 'unordered': true flag, and the four stats stored in an unordered coreSet. The Legion-grid justification was DELETED as a cross-system inference the source does not make. The class-specific Critical Rate overflow rule is preserved in a separate afterCoreSet object because the doc DOES state it as sequential ('after filling out the usual big 4') and gives a figure ('running between 7-10 Crit Rate is advisable'), both re-verified verbatim. A matching entry was added to commonMistakes so the refusal-to-rank is surfaced to users rather than papered over.

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.what: vMatrix priority was restructured from a flat skill ranking to the six numbered node groups the sources actually use.
correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: Re-reading the class doc produced its operative sentence verbatim: 'It is mandatory to level the first four nodes to maximum. Node 5 for Covering Fire/Swift Surge is optional for mains looking to minmax and not necessary for 6th job progression. Node 6 is completely useless at all times.' Nodes are PAIRS, and the doc's own Node 5 and Node 6 match Grandis's Node 5 and Node 6 exactly. So 'the mandatory four' means node groups 1-4 (eight skills), not four individual skills. The old file demoted Quiver Cartridge, Phoenix, Gritty Gust and Speed Mirage to a second band 'below the mandatory four' - that was a misreading that would have told players to under-level four mandatory-max nodes. Grandis's Primary(1-2)/Secondary(3-4) buckets are a within-mandatory ordering, not a demotion.

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.what: Grandis Library was demoted from an independent corroborating source to a same-family mirror for boost nodes, hyper passives and inner ability.
correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: Its Credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc'. The old file counted 'PRIMARY on Grandis Library' as corroboration of the class doc's node ranking and rated several claims 'moderate' on that basis. Every affected claim now carries a sourceCountNote naming the family collapse, and sourceCount counts families rather than URLs. Grandis's skill tables, Base Stats and node membership lists remain independent because they are API-derived and outside that credit.

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.what: The 'training' role labels on mastermysty's second and third trios were deleted.
correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: Re-reading the source shows it labels only the first Bow Master trio, as 'Bossing'. The others are headed 'Trio #2' and 'Trio #3' with no role label at all. The old file's 'second (training) trio' and 'third, training-oriented trio' were inferences presented as source claims. Both now read role: 'unlabelled' with a roleSource field saying exactly what the source does and does not say.

That page is outside the 'Class Doc' credit, so the claim keeps its genuinely independent second lane and its 'moderate' rating on a source that was actually read.

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: Grandis Library's training substitution names only 'Arrow Stream - Reinforce and Extra Strike'. The class doc lists Spread among available Arrow Stream passives with its effect (Max Monsters Hit +1) but does not put it in a recommended loadout. It now sits in a new availableButNotRecommended bucket alongside Sharp Eyes - Persist, which has the same status.

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.what: Two unverifiable glosses were deleted from hexa.order: Charon described as 'a death-prevention effect', and the HEXA Stat advice about rearranging rolls so the largest value sits on the highest-priority line.
correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: Neither could be found on re-reading the class doc. The doc says only 'At Lv. 20, you gain access to Sol Hecate: Charon' and 'ATT > DEX > Boss%'. A previously-unrecorded doc instruction WAS found and added instead: 'Styx should be registered to Terms & Conditions and Phlegethon should be registered to Vicious Shot.'

correctionsFoundDuringResolution.what: The HEXA node prerequisites (Mastery needs boost nodes Lv. 40+, Enhancement needs job nodes Lv. 25+) were promoted from a hedged aside in hexa.notes to a structured hexa.prerequisites field with the doc's verbatim wording.
correctionsFoundDuringResolution.why: The old file flagged them as an unchecked text-extraction artifact. They were re-read directly this session and are the class doc's actual wording. Still single-sourced and labelled weak, since they have not been checked against an in-game mechanics page.

blockedReason: All six contested defects were settled - one out of scope, five corrected or confirmed - and every claim in the five endgame sections now carries re-verified sources, a family-counted sourceCount, a consensus label and verifiedAt 2026-09-12. Two items remain genuinely unresolved and are recorded as conflicts rather than as claims, which is why this stays false: (1) whether the Final Attack boost node targets 'Final Attack: Bow' or 'Advanced Final Attack' - MapleStory Wiki confirms these are two distinct real skills, and the disagreement changes what a player is told to level; (2) the class doc's own Node 1-4 skill membership, which is image-encoded and produced three mutually inconsistent text extractions this session, so the file ships Grandis Library's pairing under a flag. Both need a vision pass on the class doc's boost node infographic. Separately, hyperSkills.actives is still unsourced and null. Nothing unverified is presented as guidance, but the vMatrix section cannot be called settled until the node membership is read from the images.
